research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register text of Executive Order 14006 of January 26, 2021, Reforming Our Incarceration System To Eliminate the Use of Privately Operated Criminal Detention Facilities (86 FR 7483, PDF pages 1-2 of the 2021-01-29 issue, FR Doc. 2021-02070), matching the census register row (2021-01-26, Joseph R. Biden Jr.). I read the whole held text; the page identification is taken from the held text's own header, not from a page image. Inventory: the dossier's seven scopes (sec1, sec2, sec3, sec3-i, sec3-i-ii, sec3-b, sec3-c) run from section 1 to section 3(c) and the signature, and no operative sentence lies outside them; I confirm the inventory without change. The order has one operative command, section 2 (the Attorney General is not to renew Department of Justice contracts with privately operated criminal detention facilities, as consistent with applicable law), with no deadline, condition, sunset, report or term. Ending: Executive Order 14148 of January 20, 2025, section 2(q), lists this order among the executive actions that are 'are hereby revoked:' It has no delayed-effect wording and no exception or saving for this order, so every scope ended on its signing date, January 20, 2025; the alternative reading, its Federal Register publication on January 28, 2025, would only move the date. The by-number search of held texts (the six texts in the packet lookups are four copies of EO 14148 and two of this order) and the three machine searches found no statute, court action, expiry or other instrument acting on this order, so the revocation is the first end of every scope and the whole-order end. The OLRC note at 18 U.S.C. 4013 note reports the same revocation. The order was therefore not operative on the 2026-10-14 cutoff; provisional status NO is unchanged. The original is the official FR text layer; no working-text substitute is used.

research_rationale: Identity: the registered original is Executive Order 5825 of March 26, 1932, Leaves of Absence, Foreign Service, held as the official compilation Proclamations and Executive Orders: Herbert Hoover, vol. II (OFR/GPO 1974), printed page 1115, PDF page 344 (OCR text layer of the scan, grade official_compilation_high; the order predates the Federal Register). The census register row (1932-03-26, Herbert Hoover) and the WPA 1944 list entry for March 26, 1932 (page 501, amending the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers and the Consular Regulations on leave without compensation) agree. The page identification comes from the held text's own header; I did not view the page image. I read the whole held text: one enacting sentence amending paragraph (d) of section 8, chapter VI, of the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers and paragraph (d) of section 467 of the Consular Regulations of 1896, and the new paragraph (d), Leave without compensation. The dossier's two scopes (lead, d) cover it; I confirm the inventory. Ending: Executive Order 8189 of July 5, 1939 (4 FR 2783, Federal Register of July 7, 1939) lists this order under the heading 'Revocation of Executive Orders'. The same order cancels listed provisions of the Foreign Service Regulations and adds a new section on leaves of absence, so the revocation comes with a replacement. EO 8189 has no delayed-effect wording; the sentences 'This order shall become effective on July 1, 1939' on the same Federal Register page belong to the orders that follow its signature block, EOs 8190 and 8191. The end is therefore its signing date, July 5, 1939 (its filing on July 6 and publication on July 7, 1939 are the alternative readings). Machine searches reported no hits for the number 5825, so the revocation comes from the by-number search of held texts and my reading of EO 8189. No earlier end: I read the held orders of 1932-1939 amending the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers or the Consular Regulations (EOs 6737, 6810, 7012, 7013, 7261, 7449); none touches leave of absence. The order was not operative on 2026-10-14; provisional status NO is unchanged. The text rests on an OCR layer of an official compilation, not a human transcription.

Nothing held shows rights or acts accrued under EO 5825 that were saved.

EOs of 1932-1939 amending the Instructions or Consular Regulations (6737, 6810, 7012, 7013, 7261, 7449) deal with other subjects (organization of the Department, drafts, office hours and precedence, hostesses, inventories) and do not touch leave without compensation.
